The graph of $y=f(x),$ shown above, consists of three line segments. Find the value of ${\int }_{-5}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$
questions.worked_solution:
We divide the interval of integration into $4$ regions: the line segment for $x\in [-5,-3],$ the line segment for $x\in [-3,-1],$ the line segment for $x\in (-1,1),$ and the line segment for $x\in [1,4].$ Therefore, we can write the required integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-5}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-5}^{-3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-3}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}+{{{\int }_{1}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{4}}
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-5,-3].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2\cdot 2) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-3,-1].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2\cdot 2) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have

$$
{\int }_{-4}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{2}=-2.
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (-1,1).$ The corresponding region is a square, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & ={s}^{2} \\  & ={2}^{2} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $4$th integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [1,4].$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{4} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(3\cdot 3) \\  & =4.5.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have

$$
{\int }_{1}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{4}=-4.5.
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-5}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}-{A}_{2}+{A}_{3}-{A}_{4} \\  & =2-2+4-4.5 \\  & =-0.5.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-4,-1].$ The corresponding region is a rectangle, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =bh \\  & =3\cdot 2 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (-1,0].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle below the $x$-axis, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1\cdot 1) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we subtract its area.

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [0,3].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so

$$

Given the graph of $y=f(x)$ above, find the value of 
${\int }_{-4}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$
questions.worked_solution:
The graph consists of $2$ parts: the arc of the semi-circle for $x\in [-4,0]$ and the line segment for $x\in (0,3).$ So, we can use the additive property of integrals to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-4}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={{{\int }_{-4}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{0}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-4,0].$ The corresponding region is a combination of a semi-circle of radius $2$ and a rectangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(\pi {r}^{2})+bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\pi \cdot {2}^{2})+4(2) \\  & =2\pi +8.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (0,3).$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1+3)(3) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =(2\pi +8)+6 \\  & =2\pi +14.\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\pi \cdot {2}^{2} \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
{\int }_{-1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{2}=-2\pi .
$$

The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (3,5].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
{\int }_{3}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{3}=-2.
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-5}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}-{A}_{2}-{A}_{3} \\  & =8-2\pi -2 \\  & =6-2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14010574/assets/ad45cbdcd126df931f1a35c60ca12b45d520a2a0a5cddf4fa012c0515d3024c7.png)

The graph of $y=f(x),$ shown above, consists of two line segments. Find the value of $\displaystyle \int_{0}^{4} f(x)\: \textrm{d}x.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The graph consists of two parts: the line segment for $x \in [0,2)$ and the line segment for $x \in [2,4].$ Therefore, we can write the required integral as follows:

$$
\int_{0}^{4} f(x)\: \textrm{d}x = \underbrace{\int_{0}^{2} f(x)\: \textrm{d}x}_{A_1} + \underbrace{\int_{2}^{4} f(x)\: \textrm{d}x}_{-A_2}.
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in [0,2).$ The corresponding region is a rectangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =bh \\  & =2\cdot 2 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in [2,4].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
\int_{2}^{4} f(x)\: \textrm{d}x =-A_2 = -2.
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}-{A}_{2} \\  & =4-2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14010574/assets/36c6a1c84e0b0c32a5fd35fd422645f60340da6d205dd8cc31054cd558c2f5f9.png)

Given the graph of $y=f(x)$ above, find the value of $\displaystyle \int_{-4}^4 f(x) \,\textrm{d}x.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The graph consists of four parts: the arc of a semi-circle for $x\in [-4,0],$ a line segment for $x\in (0,2),$ a line segment for $x\in (2,4],$ and the point at $x=2.$ So, we can use the additive property of integrals to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-4}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={{{\int }_{-4}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{2}}+0+{{{\int }_{2}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in [-4,0].$ The corresponding region is a semi-circle with a radius of $2,$ so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \pi \cdot {2}^{2} \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in (0,2).$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have

$$
\int_{0}^{2} f(x)\: \textrm{d}x = -A_2 = -2.
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in (2,4].$  The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}-{A}_{2}+{A}_{3} \\  & =2\pi -2+2 \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
